sentence: You can't use the lift yet. It ___ by an engineer.
setupText: Choose the passive form describing work in progress now.
taskText: You can't use the lift yet. It ___ by an engineer.
text: Choose the passive form describing work in progress now. You can't use the lift yet. It ___ by an engineer.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2321:Present continuous passive for current work
explanation: Is being serviced is present continuous passive; the engineer is working on the lift now.

rationales.has serviced: Has serviced makes the lift the engineer's role: an active performer of servicing.
rationales.is being serviced: Is being serviced is present continuous passive; the engineer is working on the lift now.
rationales.is servicing: Is servicing is active continuous and would make the lift service something else.
rationales.was serviced: Was serviced reports past work rather than the current work that explains its unavailability.

sentence: There is no space on the tour because all twenty places ___.
setupText: Choose the form reporting completed reservations that explain the situation now.
taskText: There is no space on the tour because all twenty places ___.
text: Choose the form reporting completed reservations that explain the situation now. There is no space on the tour because all twenty places ___.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2322:Present perfect passive for a current result
explanation: Have been reserved is present perfect passive; completed reservations explain the lack of space now.

rationales.have reserved: Have reserved is active and would make the places perform reservations.
rationales.are reserving: Are reserving also makes the places the actors and presents activity rather than completed reservations.
rationales.were reserving: Were reserving is active past continuous, not a completed passive result.
rationales.have been reserved: Have been reserved is present perfect passive; completed reservations explain the lack of space now.

sentence: The young trees ___ when heavy rain forced the volunteers to stop.
setupText: Choose the form showing that planting was already in progress when the rain started.
taskText: The young trees ___ when heavy rain forced the volunteers to stop.
text: Choose the form showing that planting was already in progress when the rain started. The young trees ___ when heavy rain forced the volunteers to stop.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2323:Past continuous passive as interrupted background
explanation: Were being planted places the trees as receivers of an activity underway at the past interruption.

rationales.were being planted: Were being planted places the trees as receivers of an activity underway at the past interruption.
rationales.had planted: Had planted is active and makes the trees the planters; it also looks back at prior completion.
rationales.have been planted: Have been planted reports a result up to now rather than an activity underway at that past moment.
rationales.were planting: Were planting is active and makes the trees perform the planting.

sentence: When I phoned the campsite, the last cabin ___, so I booked a tent space instead.
setupText: Choose the passive form explicitly placing the booking before my call.
taskText: When I phoned the campsite, the last cabin ___, so I booked a tent space instead.
text: Choose the passive form explicitly placing the booking before my call. When I phoned the campsite, the last cabin ___, so I booked a tent space instead.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2324:Past perfect passive before another past event
explanation: Had been booked places a completed booking before the past call and keeps the cabin as its receiver.

rationales.has booked: Has booked is active and would make the cabin the booking agent.
rationales.was booking: Was booking is active continuous; it neither places the cabin as receiver nor marks the earlier completed booking.
rationales.had been booked: Had been booked places a completed booking before the past call and keeps the cabin as its receiver.
rationales.has been booking: Has been booking is active perfect continuous and gives the cabin an ongoing booking role.

sentence: The paint should ___ away from direct sunlight.
setupText: Choose the form giving advice about what people should do with the paint.
taskText: The paint should ___ away from direct sunlight.
text: Choose the form giving advice about what people should do with the paint. The paint should ___ away from direct sunlight.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2325:Should in a passive recommendation
explanation: Should be stored is a passive recommendation: someone should keep the paint in the stated conditions.

rationales.store it: Store it is active and repeats the paint as an object while making it the storing agent.
rationales.be stored: Should be stored is a passive recommendation: someone should keep the paint in the stated conditions.
rationales.being stored: Should requires the base form be, not being, before stored.
rationales.have stored: Should have stored is active perfect and makes the paint the actor; it does not give the intended advice about what people should do with it.

sentence: Travel passes ___ to the inspector on request.
setupText: Choose the form stating a requirement for passengers.
taskText: Travel passes ___ to the inspector on request.
text: Choose the form stating a requirement for passengers. Travel passes ___ to the inspector on request.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2326:Have to with a plural passive subject
explanation: Have to be shown expresses a requirement while making the passes the things shown to the inspector.

rationales.have to show: Have to show is active and makes the passes the people showing something.
rationales.has to be shown: Has does not agree with the plural subject travel passes.
rationales.have to showing: After have to, the passive uses be shown, not showing.
rationales.have to be shown: Have to be shown expresses a requirement while making the passes the things shown to the inspector.

sentence: The host offered us a quieter table.
setupText: Choose the passive sentence keeping 'us' as the people receiving the offer.
taskText: The host offered us a quieter table.
text: Choose the passive sentence keeping 'us' as the people receiving the offer. The host offered us a quieter table.
options: We offered the host a quieter table.
The host was offered our quieter table.
We were offered a quieter table.
We were offering a quieter table.
answer: We were offered a quieter table.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2327:Recipient subject in a double-object passive
explanation: 'We' becomes the passive subject as the recipient of the host's offer; the offered table stays in the sentence.

'We' becomes the passive subject as the recipient of the host's offer; the offered table stays in the sentence.
This makes us the people offering something and the host its recipient.
This makes the host receive an offer of our table, reversing the original offer to us.
'Were offering' is active continuous and makes us the offerers rather than recipients.

sentence: The supplier sent the customer a replacement battery.
setupText: Choose the passive version beginning with 'the replacement battery' and preserving the recipient.
taskText: The supplier sent the customer a replacement battery.
text: Choose the passive version beginning with 'the replacement battery' and preserving the recipient. The supplier sent the customer a replacement battery.
options: A replacement battery was sent to the customer.
A replacement battery was sent by the customer.
A replacement battery sent the customer to the supplier.
A replacement battery was sending the customer.
answer: A replacement battery was sent to the customer.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2328:Thing subject with a retained to-recipient phrase
explanation: When the battery is the passive subject, 'to the customer' preserves the recipient of the supplier's sending.

rationales.A replacement battery was sent by the cu: 'By the customer' makes the customer the sender, reversing the original recipient role.
rationales.A replacement battery sent the customer: This makes the battery act and turns the supplier into a destination.
rationales.A replacement battery was sent to the cu: When the battery is the passive subject, 'to the customer' preserves the recipient of the supplier's sending.
rationales.A replacement battery was sending the cu: 'Was sending' is active continuous and makes the battery the sender.

sentence: The noise complaint will ___ next week.
setupText: Choose the passive phrase meaning the council will investigate the complaint.
taskText: The noise complaint will ___ next week.
text: Choose the passive phrase meaning the council will investigate the complaint. The noise complaint will ___ next week.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2329:Retaining a preposition in a passive phrasal expression
explanation: Be looked into is the passive of look into. Keep into because it is part of the investigation expression.

rationales.be looked: Looked needs into to retain the investigate meaning of look into.
rationales.look into: Look into is active and would make the complaint investigate something.
rationales.be looking into: Be looking into is active continuous rather than passive.
rationales.be looked into: Be looked into is the passive of look into. Keep into because it is part of the investigation expression.

sentence: Someone collects recycling from these bins every Wednesday. The notice is about the collection schedule.
setupText: Choose the concise notice preserving the collection rule without inventing a collector.
taskText: Someone collects recycling from these bins every Wednesday. The notice is about the collection schedule.
text: Choose the concise notice preserving the collection rule without inventing a collector. Someone collects recycling from these bins every Wednesday. The notice is about the collection schedule.
options: Recycling is collected from these bins every Wednesday.
The caretaker collects these bins every Wednesday.
These bins collect recycling from Wednesday.
Recycling is collected only when the bins are full.
answer: Recycling is collected from these bins every Wednesday.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2330:Agent omission for a schedule-focused notice
explanation: The passive keeps the recycling and schedule prominent while leaving the unspecified collector unnamed.

rationales.The caretaker collects these bins every: The source does not identify the caretaker and says recycling, not the bins themselves, is collected.
rationales.Recycling is collected from these bins e: The passive keeps the recycling and schedule prominent while leaving the unspecified collector unnamed.
rationales.These bins collect recycling from Wednes: This changes collection into a function of the bins and replaces a weekly schedule with a starting point.
rationales.Recycling is collected only when the bin: This replaces the stated weekly schedule with a fullness condition that was not supplied.

sentence: I don't enjoy ___ while I am explaining a problem.
setupText: Choose the form meaning other people interrupt me.
taskText: I don't enjoy ___ while I am explaining a problem.
text: Choose the form meaning other people interrupt me. I don't enjoy ___ while I am explaining a problem.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2331:Passive gerund after enjoy
explanation: Being interrupted is a passive -ing form; I receive the interruption from someone else.

rationales.being interrupted: Being interrupted is a passive -ing form; I receive the interruption from someone else.
rationales.interrupting someone: Interrupting someone makes me the person who interrupts, reversing the intended role.
rationales.having interrupted: Having interrupted describes my earlier action as the interrupter, not an interruption I receive.
rationales.be interrupted: Enjoy takes an -ing form here, so the passive must be being interrupted.

sentence: After completing the training, I hope ___ to team leader.
setupText: Choose the form meaning the company may promote me.
taskText: After completing the training, I hope ___ to team leader.
text: Choose the form meaning the company may promote me. After completing the training, I hope ___ to team leader.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2332:Passive infinitive after hope
explanation: To be promoted is a passive infinitive, placing me as the person receiving the hoped-for promotion.

rationales.promoting: Hope normally takes a to-infinitive here, and promoting would make me the actor.
rationales.to promote: To promote makes me the person promoting someone else; the intended meaning is that I receive promotion.
rationales.to be promoted: To be promoted is a passive infinitive, placing me as the person receiving the hoped-for promotion.
rationales.being promote: Being promote combines being with a base form and does not fit after hope.

sentence: The instructor explained the safety rule to us.
setupText: Choose the standard British English passive preserving what was explained and to whom.
taskText: The instructor explained the safety rule to us.
text: Choose the standard British English passive preserving what was explained and to whom. The instructor explained the safety rule to us.
options: The safety rule was explained to us.
We were explained the safety rule.
The safety rule was explained by us.
We were explaining the safety rule.
answer: The safety rule was explained to us.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2333:Explain with a content subject and to-recipient
explanation: The rule becomes the passive subject, and to us keeps the people who received the explanation.

In standard British English, explain takes the content as its direct object; make the rule the passive subject and retain to us.
The rule becomes the passive subject, and to us keeps the people who received the explanation.
By us makes us the explainers rather than the people receiving the explanation.
Were explaining is active continuous and makes us the instructors.

sentence: Describe the guests reaching the venue just after six.
setupText: Choose the correct arrival statement in contemporary standard British English.
taskText: Describe the guests reaching the venue just after six.
text: Choose the correct arrival statement in contemporary standard British English. Describe the guests reaching the venue just after six.
options: The guests were arrived just after six.
The guests arrived just after six.
The guests were arrive just after six.
The guests did arrived just after six.
answer: The guests arrived just after six.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2334:Avoiding passive marking with intransitive arrive
explanation: Arrived is active and intransitive: the guests reach the venue without receiving an action from a separate agent.

In contemporary standard British English, arrive does not form an ordinary passive with were arrived in this meaning.
Were cannot directly combine with the base form arrive in this statement.
Did requires the base form arrive, not arrived.
Arrived is active and intransitive: the guests reach the venue without receiving an action from a separate agent.

sentence: My colleague got promoted after leading the successful launch.
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'got promoted' in this informal account.
taskText: My colleague got promoted after leading the successful launch.
text: Choose the meaning of 'got promoted' in this informal account. My colleague got promoted after leading the successful launch.
options: The colleague arranged a launch for a promoted worker.
The colleague lost a promotion after the launch.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2335:Beneficial event in an informal get-passive
explanation: 'Got promoted' is an informal get-passive: someone promoted the colleague.

'Got promoted' is an informal get-passive: someone promoted the colleague.
'Got promoted' makes the colleague the recipient, not the person promoting others.
rationales.The colleague arranged a launch for a pr: The phrase describes the colleague's promotion, not the status of another worker.
rationales.The colleague lost a promotion after the: 'Got promoted' states a successful promotion, not its loss; get-passives need not describe bad events.

sentence: I paid a tailor to shorten these trousers.
setupText: Choose the statement saying a tailor did the alteration for me.
taskText: I paid a tailor to shorten these trousers.
text: Choose the statement saying a tailor did the alteration for me. I paid a tailor to shorten these trousers.
options: I had shortened these trousers before paying.
I had these trousers to shorten.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2336:Causative have with an affected object and participle
explanation: Had these trousers shortened uses have plus object plus participle to describe arranging work by someone else.

Myself says I performed the alteration, contrary to the tailor doing it.
rationales.I had shortened these trousers before pa: Had shortened is active past perfect and makes me the person who completed the shortening.
Had these trousers shortened uses have plus object plus participle to describe arranging work by someone else.
Had these trousers to shorten gives me a task to perform, not an alteration performed for me.

sentence: Bags ___ in front of the emergency exit.
setupText: Choose the passive prohibition that says users must keep this exit clear.
taskText: Bags ___ in front of the emergency exit.
text: Choose the passive prohibition that says users must keep this exit clear. Bags ___ in front of the emergency exit.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2337:Negative modal passive prohibition
explanation: Must not be left prohibits people from placing or leaving bags in that location.

rationales.must not leave them: This active phrase makes bags the people leaving something and repeats them as an object.
rationales.must not be leaving: Be leaving is active continuous, not a passive about bags placed by people.
rationales.must be not leaving: Be not leaving remains active continuous and does not form the required prohibition about bags.
rationales.must not be left: Must not be left prohibits people from placing or leaving bags in that location.

sentence: At the airport desk, ask about your suitcase.
setupText: Choose the passive question asking whether the weighing is complete.
taskText: At the airport desk, ask about your suitcase.
text: Choose the passive question asking whether the weighing is complete. At the airport desk, ask about your suitcase.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2338:Present perfect passive question
explanation: Has ... been weighed is present perfect passive and asks whether the weighing has occurred.

rationales.Has the suitcase been weighed?: Has ... been weighed is present perfect passive and asks whether the weighing has occurred.
rationales.Has the suitcase been weighing?: Been weighing forms an active progressive and does not place the suitcase as the thing weighed.
rationales.Has the suitcase being weighed?: After has, the passive perfect requires been, not being.
rationales.Have the suitcase been weighed?: The singular suitcase requires has, not have.

sentence: The footpath was blocked by fallen branches after the storm.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that does not turn the cause into an unidentified person.
taskText: The footpath was blocked by fallen branches after the storm.
text: Choose the interpretation that does not turn the cause into an unidentified person. The footpath was blocked by fallen branches after the storm.
options: A person deliberately used the branches to block the path.
The footpath caused the branches to fall.
Fallen branches caused the blockage; no person's action is stated.
The storm was blocked by the footpath.
answer: Fallen branches caused the blockage; no person's action is stated.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2339:Nonhuman cause in a passive by phrase
explanation: A passive by phrase can identify a nonhuman cause. The sentence does not establish a person acting deliberately.

rationales.A person deliberately used the branches: The by phrase names a cause, but it does not state deliberate action by a person.
rationales.The footpath caused the branches to fall: This reverses the relation: the branches block the path, not the path causing their fall.
rationales.Fallen branches caused the blockage; no: A passive by phrase can identify a nonhuman cause. The sentence does not establish a person acting deliberately.
The storm supplies the setting, not the thing blocked in the passive sentence.

sentence: Workers ___ each delivery, and damaged goods ___ immediately.
setupText: Choose the pair keeping workers as inspectors and damaged goods as receivers of removal.
taskText: Workers ___ each delivery, and damaged goods ___ immediately.
text: Choose the pair keeping workers as inspectors and damaged goods as receivers of removal. Workers ___ each delivery, and damaged goods ___ immediately.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b1-2340:Switching voice when the grammatical subject changes role
explanation: Inspect is active because workers do the checking; are removed is passive because the goods receive the removal action.

rationales.are inspected / remove: Are inspected makes workers the receivers, while remove makes damaged goods the actors; both roles are reversed.
rationales.inspect / are removed: Inspect is active because workers do the checking; are removed is passive because the goods receive the removal action.
rationales.inspect / are removing: Are removing makes the damaged goods remove something rather than be removed.
rationales.are inspecting / have removed: Have removed makes the goods the active removers and changes the routine result into an active completed action.
